title: Greedy Best-First in San Francisco: Rush or Route?
description: Watch Greedy Best-First Search on a real city-style grid: it uses only the heuristic to “speed-walk” toward the goal. Then compare how/why it can fail when the closest-looking route leads into dead ends.
ig_caption:
Greedy Best-First Search vs A*: Pathfinding Comparison — Why it rushes to the goal ⚡ and when it fails.

In this Mission District map, Greedy Best-First always expands the node with the smallest h(n) (heuristic-to-goal). That means it’s fast to *look smart*—but it doesn’t consider the path cost so it can ignore smarter detours.

Mechanics you’ll see in the animation:
• Priority queue ordered by h(n) only
• It “commits” early because the heuristic dominates
• It can get trapped when the heuristic is misleading (local minimum)

✅ Takeaway: Greedy Best-First is a great heuristic-driven explorer, but it’s not guaranteed optimal.

Debate question: If you had to choose one for real-time routing—Greedy Best-First (fast) or A* (safer)—which would you ship and why?
